class.name: PhysXCloth3D
class.brief_description: A simulated cloth patch, provided by the PhysX module.
class.description: Simulates a rectangular grid (or a supplied triangle mesh) as cloth and draws the result as an [ArrayMesh]. The simulation runs on a built-in extended position-based-dynamics (XPBD) solver on the CPU, so it works on any platform; the GPU deformable-surface path is used when the PhysX backend has GPU support available. The cloth collides with the rest of the physics world through [PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D] queries (independent of which 3D physics engine is active) and reacts to the wind of an [Area3D] assigned to [member wind_area]. Fix parts of the cloth in place with [member pin_mode], [member pinned_vertices] or a moving [member anchor_path].

method.name: get_vertex_count
method.description: Returns the number of simulated vertices.

method.name: is_gpu_accelerated
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the GPU deformable-surface path is in use rather than the CPU XPBD fallback.

method.name: reset
method.description: Drops the cloth back to its rest shape at the node's current transform.

members.member: Optional [Node3D] the pinned vertices follow: as it moves and rotates, so do the pins, so the cloth can hang off an animated object.
Resistance to folding, from 0 (limp) to 1 (stiff). Low values give soft, drapey cloth.
When enabled, each vertex is pushed out of any physics body it overlaps each step.
Fraction of a vertex's sideways velocity removed while it is touching a surface, from 0 (frictionless) to 1. Higher values stop the cloth sliding and spinning once it settles.
Physics layers the cloth collides with.
Fraction of velocity removed per second. Raises to settle the cloth faster.
Areal mass in kg/m², used to weight the vertices. Heavier cloth swings less in the wind.
How hard air pushes on a triangle face-on. Drives the billow.
Vertices across the generated grid. Ignored when [member source_mesh] is set.
Vertices down the generated grid. Ignored when [member source_mesh] is set.
Size of the generated grid in meters, centered on the node in its local XY plane (facing +Z).
Sideways push from air flowing across a triangle, which makes slack cloth ripple.
A quick way to fix an edge or the corners of a generated grid in place.
Extra vertices to fix in place, by index, on top of [member pin_mode].
Resistance to in-plane skewing, from 0 to 1.
When [code]false[/code] the cloth freezes in place.

Which solver runs the cloth. [constant SIM_AUTO] uses the GPU deformable surface when a CUDA device is available and the built-in CPU solver otherwise. The GPU option is hidden in the inspector on machines without CUDA; a scene saved with it still loads elsewhere and falls back to the CPU solver. See [method is_gpu_accelerated].
A triangle mesh to simulate instead of a generated grid. Its first surface is used.
Resistance to stretching along the weave, from 0 (elastic) to 1 (inextensible).
Solver substeps per physics tick. More substeps make stiff cloth more stable at some CPU cost.
A constant world-space air velocity, added on top of any [member wind_area].
An [Area3D] whose wind settings (force, source, attenuation) drive the cloth. The cloth does not need to be a physics body to use this.
Master switch for all air forces ([member wind], [member wind_area], [member drag], [member lift]).
Adds a swirling gust on top of the steady wind, as a fraction of its speed.

constants.constant: Nothing is pinned; the cloth falls freely.
The top row of a generated grid is fixed.
Only the two top corners of a generated grid are fixed.
The left column of a generated grid is fixed.
The right column of a generated grid is fixed.
GPU deformable surface when a CUDA device is present, the CPU solver otherwise.
Force the GPU deformable surface. Falls back to the CPU solver (with a configuration warning) when no CUDA device is available.
Always use the built-in CPU solver, even when a GPU is available.
